rows.selection_reason: No experiments have been completed, so there is no evidence favoring any RNA encoder, profile setting, aggregation, image encoder, or fusion method. The main uncertainty is the baseline performance of the simplest RNA-only model. config_001 tests a minimal, low-risk single-profile PCA baseline without introducing multiprofile aggregation, learned encoders, or image/fusion confounds. It is the best next experiment because it is cheap and robust, establishes a reference validation accuracy, and enables clean later comparisons to multiprofile, learned RNA encoders, image-only, and multimodal configurations under a limited budget.

The only completed experiment is an RNA-only single-profile PCA baseline with validation accuracy 0.485, so there is currently no evidence about whether image features are useful or whether multimodal fusion is worth pursuing. config_010 tests a simple image-only single-profile ResNet-50 baseline, isolating the value of the image modality without adding multiprofile aggregation or fusion. This is the best next experiment because it reduces a major uncertainty at low complexity and will guide whether subsequent budget should go toward multimodal models, stronger image encoders, or RNA/profile improvements.

RNA-only PCA with a single profile is much stronger than image-only ResNet, so the current promising direction is RNA-based modeling. It is still unclear whether multiprofile aggregation improves over the single-profile baseline; config_002 tests this by keeping the same PCA encoder and using the simplest aggregation, avgpool. This isolates the effect of multiprofile aggregation before testing more complex transformer aggregation or multimodal fusion, making it an efficient next step under a limited budget.

RNA-only multiprofile PCA with avgpool (config_002) is currently the strongest result, clearly outperforming singleprofile RNA and image-only ResNet50, so the main uncertainty is whether transformer aggregation can improve on avgpool for this promising branch. config_003 changes only aggregation, isolating that effect while keeping the best-known RNA encoder and profile setting. This is the most efficient next step because it exploits the strongest evidence, tests a key design choice with a one-variable comparison, and informs whether future multimodal configurations should use transformer or avgpool aggregation.

RNA-only multiprofile PCA with avgpool is the current strongest setting (0.591 accuracy, 0.573 F1), while image-only ResNet is weak and transformer aggregation underperforms avgpool for PCA. The key untested factor in this promising unimodal setting is RNA representation. config_008 tests scGPT while keeping profile setting and aggregation fixed, directly clarifying whether a stronger RNA encoder can improve the best baseline before adding multimodal complexity.

The strongest evidence is RNA-only multiprofile PCA with avgpool (0.591 acc), while image-only ResNet50 is weak (0.208), leaving uncertainty about whether image provides complementary signal. config_018 keeps the best RNA profile/aggregation and adds ResNet50 with simple concat fusion, directly testing the fusion/model-setting effect without changing the RNA encoder or aggregation. This is the best next step because it exploits the best unimodal direction while efficiently determining whether multimodal complexity is warranted before tuning fusion or image encoders.

Existing evidence shows RNA multiprofile avgpool with PCA is strong, and adding ResNet50 image features with concat fusion gives the current best result, but image-only ResNet50 is weak, so the value and combination of the image branch remain uncertain. config_019 changes only fusion from concat to weighted in the current best setting, isolating the fusion effect. It tests whether weighted fusion can improve on concat by better balancing RNA and image signals, or whether concat is already sufficient. This is a low-risk, one-factor extension of the most promising direction and efficiently reduces uncertainty before exploring larger changes such as new image encoders.

The strongest evidence is that multiprofile RNA with avgpool and weighted fusion is currently best, especially config_019 at 0.639 accuracy. The main uncertainty is whether the image modality contributes meaningfully, since image-only ResNet50 was weak and no ViT image encoder has been tested. config_025 keeps the current best RNA encoder, profile, aggregation, and fusion while replacing ResNet50 with imagenet_vit_l, isolating the effect of image representation. This is a high-value next experiment because it either improves on the best known configuration or clarifies whether the image branch is adding useful information under the strongest known setup.

The strongest evidence so far favors multimodal multiprofile PCA with ResNet50, avgpool, and weighted fusion, with config_019 as the current best (accuracy 0.639, F1 0.620). Weighted fusion slightly outperformed concat, and ResNet50 and ViT-L are nearly tied, so the main unresolved choice in this promising family is aggregation: avgpool beat transformer in RNA-only PCA, but it is untested in the best multimodal setting. config_021 changes only aggregation from config_019, isolating whether transformer aggregation can help once image features are fused. This is the best next experiment because it is a clean, single-change extension of the current best direction and will either reveal a better aggregation strategy or confirm avgpool, efficiently reducing uncertainty under a limited budget.

The strongest evidence so far favors multimodal multiprofile PCA + ResNet50 with avgpool and weighted fusion, reaching 0.639 accuracy and 0.620 F1, while multiprofile RNA-only PCA avgpool also substantially outperformed singleprofile RNA-only PCA. The key uncertainty is whether multiprofile aggregation is still necessary when image features are included. config_017 keeps the best-known PCA/ResNet50/weighted-fusion setup but switches to singleprofile, cleanly testing the profile-setting effect. This is a high-value experiment under a limited budget because it can either confirm that multiprofile aggregation is essential or show that a simpler singleprofile multimodal model is nearly as good, helping decide where to invest remaining experiments.
